questions.sampleAnswer: A reduction in global protection levels is likely to increase demand for Australian exports like agricultural items and services. Lower global protection levels can also promote global growth leading to higher demand for Australian mining resources. These changes would increase the value of credit entries in the BOGS, resulting in a smaller BOGS deficit or larger BOGS surplus. However, these changes would likely result in higher company profits and therefore also an increase in profits returned to foreign owners of companies in Australia, particularly from the mining sector. This will result in an increase in the value of debit entries recorded in the Net Primary Income section of the current account.

questions.sampleAnswer: Higher prices of Australian goods and services relative to the rest of the world will reduce Australia’s international competitiveness. This is because the cost of inputs sourced in Australia will be relatively higher making Australian-made products more expensive. As a result, this will reduce demand for Australian exports and increase import expenditure by Australia.

questions.sampleAnswer: An increase in the minimum wage may lead to an increase in demand pull inflation as people have higher incomes and will be able to demand more goods and services, putting upward pressure on prices. Labour market policies such as training and education that increase the skills of workers should help increase productivity, leading to possible decreased pressure on inflation in Australia. For example, in 2021 the delivering of the Foundation Skills Training Package provided $24M to upskill reading and writing in job seekers, resulting in increased labour supply and lowering the labour cost impact on inflation.

questions.sampleAnswer: The use of the NSW government Return and Earn scheme (RES), which is a subsidy, has been successful in managing the issue of preserving the natural environment. The scheme involves the NSW government paying a 10-cent cash payment per approved container at return points. Each container recycled no longer pollutes parks or waterways. The 2021–22 RES annual report confirms the scheme returned over 7 billion containers. The scheme has also contributed to a 25% reduction in plastic litter waste in NSW since 2019. On the other hand, not all containers used by individuals qualify for the RES subsidy. Consequently, some bottles do end up in landfill or in waterways despite the various access points offered by the RES.

questions.sampleAnswer: Globalisation can have contrasting impacts on economic development in China. For example, the rapid increase in China’s export trade and GDP as it integrated into the global economy during 2000s, averaging 10.5% between 2001–2010, enabled greater domestic investment into social infrastructure. This led to significant reductions in poverty and increases in the life expectancy to 76.7 years. Adult literacy also climbed to 96.5%. In contrast, the global restrictions on trade and travel introduced to contain the covid pandemic caused a 9.8% contraction in China’s GDP in 2020. The resultant interruptions to trade and investment opportunities caused China’s economic growth and consequently development to slow.
